title.zh: 卷九十三 列傳第二十三: 蕭惠 蕭迂魯 蕭圖玉 耶律鐸軫
title.en: Volume 93 Biographies 23: Xiao Hui, Xiao Yulu, Xiao Tuyu, Yelu Duozhen
title.raw: 卷九十三 列傳第二十三: 蕭惠 蕭迂魯 蕭圖玉 耶律鐸軫 Volume 93 Biographies 23: Xiao Hui, Xiao Yulu, Xiao Tuyu, Yelu Duozhen

sentences.zh: 蕭惠

translations.literal: Xiao Hui
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Hui

sentences.zh: （慈氏奴）〉

translations.literal: (Cishinu)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Cishinu)〉

sentences.zh: 蕭迂魯

translations.literal: Xiao Yulu
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yulu

sentences.zh: （鐸盧斡）〉

translations.literal: (Duoluwo)〉
translations.idiomatic: (Duoluwo)〉

sentences.zh: 蕭圖玉耶律鐸軫

translations.literal: Xiao Tuyu Yelu Duozhen
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Tuyu and Yelu Duozhen

sentences.zh: 蕭惠，字伯仁，小字脫古思，淳欽皇后弟阿古只五世孫。

translations.literal: Xiao Hui, styled Boren, small name Tuogusi, fifth-generation descendant of Aguzhi, younger brother of Empress Chunqin.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Hui, whose courtesy name was Boren and childhood name Tuogusi, was a fifth-generation descendant of Aguzhi, the empress's younger brother.

sentences.zh: 初以中宮親，為國舅詳穩。

translations.literal: At first, by virtue of kinship with the empress, he served as Imperial Uncle xiangwen.
translations.idiomatic: He first entered service as Imperial Uncle xiangwen through his connection to the empress.

sentences.zh: 從伯父排押征高麗，至奴古達北嶺，高麗阻險以拒，惠力戰，破之。

translations.literal: Following his uncle Paiya on campaign against Goguryeo, they reached Nuguda's North Ridge; Goguryeo blocked the passes to resist, and Hui fought vigorously and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: When he joined his uncle Paiya on the Goguryeo campaign and reached North Ridge at Nuguda, the Koreans barred the mountain passes against them; Hui fought hard and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 及攻開京，以軍律整肅聞，授契丹行宮都部署。

translations.literal: When they attacked Kaegyeong, he became known for strict military discipline and was appointed Khitan Mobile Court Chief Deployment Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During the assault on Kaegyeong he won renown for disciplined command, and was appointed chief deployment commissioner of the Khitan mobile court.

sentences.zh: 開泰二年，改南京統軍使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaitai, he was transferred to Southern Capital Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaitai year 2 he was made military commissioner of the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為右夷離畢，加同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Before long he became Right Yilibi and was additionally appointed Associate Director in the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was named Right Yilibi and given the concurrent title of associate director in the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 朝議以遼東重地，非勛戚不能鎮撫，乃命惠知東京留守事。

translations.literal: The court deliberated that Liaodong was a vital region that only men of merit and imperial kin could pacify and govern, and therefore ordered Hui to administer the Eastern Capital prefectural commissioner's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion held that Liaodong was too important to entrust to anyone but meritorious imperial kin, so Hui was assigned to oversee the Eastern Capital prefect's office.

sentences.zh: 改西北路招討使，封魏國公。

translations.literal: He was changed to Northwestern Route Pacification Commissioner and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to northwestern route pacification commissioner and created Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 太平六年，討回鶻阿薩蘭部，征兵諸路，獨阻卜酋長直剌後期，立斬以徇。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taiping, campaigning against the Aslan division of the Uyghurs, troops were levied on all routes; only the Zhibu chieftain Zhila was late, and he was immediately beheaded as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping year 6, while suppressing the Aslan Uyghurs, levies were called from every route; only the Zhibu chieftain Zhila arrived late, and Hui had him beheaded on the spot as an example.

sentences.zh: 進至甘州，攻圍三日，不克而還。

translations.literal: They advanced to Ganzhou, besieged it for three days, failed to take it, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The army pushed on to Ganzhou and besieged it for three days without success before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 時直剌之子聚兵來襲，阻卜酋長烏八密以告，惠未之信。

translations.literal: At that time Zhila's son gathered troops to attack; the Zhibu chieftain Wuba secretly reported this, but Hui did not believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Zhila's son was raising forces for a raid; the Zhibu chieftain Wuba sent word in secret, but Hui refused to credit the report.

sentences.zh: 會西阻卜叛，襲三克軍，都監涅魯古、突舉部節度使諧理、阿不呂等將兵三千來救，遇敵於可敦城西南。

translations.literal: Then the western Zhibu rebelled and struck the Sanke Army; Supervisory Commissioner Nielugu, Tuju Division Military Commissioner Xieli, Abulü, and others led three thousand troops to the rescue and met the enemy southwest of Keden City.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the western Zhibu rose in revolt and struck the Sanke army; Nielugu the supervisory commissioner, Xieli military commissioner of the Tuju division, Abulü, and others marched three thousand men to relieve them and met the enemy southwest of Keden.

sentences.zh: 諧理、阿不呂戰歿，士卒潰散。

translations.literal: Xieli and Abulü died in battle, and the soldiers broke and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Xieli and Abulü were killed in the fighting, and the troops broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 惠倉卒列陣，敵出不意攻我營。

translations.literal: Hui hastily formed ranks, and the enemy unexpectedly attacked our camp.
translations.idiomatic: Hui hurriedly drew up his lines, but the enemy took his camp by surprise.

sentences.zh: 眾請乘時奮擊，惠以我軍疲敝，未可用，弗聽。

translations.literal: The troops asked to strike vigorously while the moment lasted; Hui held that our army was exhausted and not yet fit for use, and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: His men urged an immediate counterattack, but Hui judged the army too worn down to fight and refused.

sentences.zh: 烏八請以夜斫營，惠又不許。

translations.literal: Wuba asked to raid the camp by night, and Hui again did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Wuba proposed a night raid on the enemy camp, and again Hui would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 阻卜歸，惠乃設伏兵擊之。

translations.literal: When the Zhibu withdrew, Hui then set an ambush and struck them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhibu turned back, Hui laid an ambush and attacked.

sentences.zh: 前鋒始交，敵敗走。

translations.literal: As soon as the vanguard engaged, the enemy was defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The moment the vanguard clashed, the enemy broke and ran.

sentences.zh: 惠為招討累年，屢遭侵掠，士馬疲困。

translations.literal: Hui served as pacification commissioner for many years, repeatedly suffered raids, and men and horses grew weary and distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Hui held the pacification commission for years; repeated incursions had left his men and horses worn out.

sentences.zh: 七年，左遷南京侍衛親軍馬步軍都指揮使，尋遷南京統軍使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was demoted to Southern Capital Palace Guard Cavalry and Infantry Chief Commander, and soon transferred to Southern Capital Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7 he was demoted to chief commander of the Southern Capital palace guard cavalry and infantry, then soon restored as military commissioner of the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 十三年，夏國李元昊誘山南党項諸部，帝親征。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Li Yuanhao of Xia enticed the southern Shannan Tangut tribes, and the emperor personally campaigned.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13, Li Yuanhao of Xia won over the Shannan Tangut tribes, and the emperor took the field in person.

sentences.zh: 元昊懼，請降。

translations.literal: Yuanhao feared this and requested surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the imperial advance, Yuanhao offered to submit.

sentences.zh: 惠曰：「元昊忘奕世恩，萌奸計，車駕親臨，不盡歸所掠。

translations.literal: Hui said: "Yuanhao has forgotten generations of grace, hatched treacherous designs, and yet when the imperial carriage comes in person he does not fully return what was plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "Yuanhao has forgotten generations of imperial favor and plotted treason; even with the emperor himself on campaign, he still will not return all he has taken.

sentences.zh: 天誘其衷，使彼來迎。

translations.literal: Heaven guided his heart and made them come to meet us.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has turned his heart and sent him out to meet the imperial host.

sentences.zh: 天與不圖，後悔何及？」

translations.literal: If heaven's gift is not seized, what use is regret afterward?"
translations.idiomatic: If we let heaven's offer slip away, regret will come too late."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，進軍。

translations.literal: At daybreak they advanced the army.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the army marched forward.

sentences.zh: 夏人列拒馬於河西，蔽盾以立，惠擊敗之。

translations.literal: The Xia people arrayed chevaux-de-frise west of the river and stood behind shields; Hui defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia drew up barricades west of the river and stood behind shields; Hui broke their line.

sentences.zh: 元昊走，惠麾先鋒及右翼邀之。

translations.literal: Yuanhao fled; Hui directed the vanguard and right wing to intercept him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao fled, and Hui sent the vanguard and right wing to cut him off.

sentences.zh: 夏人千餘潰圍出，我師逆擊。

translations.literal: More than a thousand Xia soldiers broke out of encirclement; our army met and struck them.
translations.idiomatic: Over a thousand Xia troops broke through the encirclement, and our forces turned to strike them.

sentences.zh: 大風忽起，飛沙瞇目，軍亂，夏人乘之，蹂踐而死者不可勝計。

translations.literal: A great wind suddenly rose, flying sand blinded the eyes, the army fell into disorder, the Xia seized the chance, and those trampled to death could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: A sudden gale whipped up blinding sand; the army fell into chaos, the Xia pressed the advantage, and countless men were trampled to death.

sentences.zh: 詔班師。

translations.literal: An edict ordered withdrawal of the army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the army to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 十七年，尚帝姊秦晉國長公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he married the emperor's elder sister, the Princess of Qin-Jin, and was appointed Commandant Escort.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he wed the emperor's elder sister, the Princess of Qin-Jin, and was made commandant escort.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝復征夏國。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor again campaigned against Xia.
translations.idiomatic: The following year the emperor marched against Xia once more.

sentences.zh: 惠自河南進，戰艦糧船綿亙數百里。

translations.literal: Hui advanced from Henan; war vessels and grain ships stretched unbroken for several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Hui advanced from Henan with a river fleet of warships and supply boats stretching for hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 既入敵境，偵候不遠，鎧甲載於車，軍士不得乘馬。

translations.literal: Once they entered enemy territory, scouts were not sent far; armor was loaded on carts, and soldiers were not permitted to mount horses.
translations.idiomatic: After crossing into enemy territory he posted scouts only close at hand, stowed armor on wagons, and kept his men off their horses.

sentences.zh: 諸將咸請備不虞，惠曰：「諒祚必自迎車駕，何暇及我？

translations.literal: All the generals jointly asked to guard against the unexpected; Hui said: "Liangzuo is sure to go out himself to meet the imperial carriage—how would he have time for us?
translations.idiomatic: The generals all urged precautions against surprise; Hui replied, "Liangzuo will surely come out to greet the emperor himself—what time will he have for us?

sentences.zh: 無故設備，徒自弊耳。」

translations.literal: To prepare without cause is merely to wear ourselves out for nothing."
translations.idiomatic: Arming for nothing would only exhaust us."

sentences.zh: 數日，我軍未營。

translations.literal: For several days our army did not encamp.
translations.idiomatic: For days the army made no camp.

sentences.zh: 候者報夏師至，惠方詰妄言罪，諒祚軍從阪而下。

translations.literal: Scouts reported the Xia army had arrived; Hui was just then questioning the offense of false report, when Liangzuo's army came down the slope.
translations.idiomatic: When scouts reported the Xia army's approach, Hui was still rebuking them for false alarm—just as Liangzuo's forces poured down the slope.

sentences.zh: 惠與麾下不及甲而走。

translations.literal: Hui and his followers had no time to don armor and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Hui and his staff fled before they could arm themselves.

sentences.zh: 追者射惠，幾不免，軍士死傷尤眾。

translations.literal: Pursuers shot at Hui and he nearly perished; among the soldiers deaths and wounds were especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuers shot at Hui and nearly killed him; the toll among the troops was especially heavy.

sentences.zh: 師還，以惠子慈氏奴歿於陣，詔釋其罪。

translations.literal: When the army returned, because Hui's son Cishinu died in battle, an edict pardoned his offense.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return, because Hui's son Cishinu had fallen in battle, the emperor pardoned his defeat.

sentences.zh: 十九年，請老，詔賜肩輿入朝，策杖上殿。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he requested retirement; an edict granted him a sedan chair to enter court and allowed him to ascend the hall leaning on a staff.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 he asked to retire; the emperor granted him a sedan chair for court audience and permission to enter the hall with a walking staff.

sentences.zh: 辭章再上，乃許之，封魏國王。

translations.literal: His memorial of resignation was submitted twice before permission was granted, and he was enfeoffed as King of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: After he petitioned twice more, retirement was granted and he was created King of Wei.

sentences.zh: 詔冬夏赴行在，參決疑議。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to come to the mobile court in winter and summer to join in resolving doubtful questions.
translations.idiomatic: He was commanded to attend the mobile court each winter and summer to help settle doubtful matters.

sentences.zh: 既歸，遣賜湯藥及他錫賚不絕。

translations.literal: After he returned home, imperial gifts of medicinal broth and other bestowments were sent without interruption.
translations.idiomatic: Once home, imperial gifts of medicine and other honors arrived in an unbroken stream.

sentences.zh: 每生日，輒賜詩以示尊寵。

translations.literal: On each birthday poems were granted to show esteem and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Each birthday brought an imperial poem testifying to his favored standing.

sentences.zh: 清寧二年薨，年七十四，遺命家人薄葬。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingning he died at seventy-four; his last testament ordered the family to bury him modestly.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Qingning year 2 at seventy-four, leaving instructions for a simple burial.

sentences.zh: 訃聞，輟朝三日。

translations.literal: When the death report arrived, court was suspended for three days.
translations.idiomatic: On news of his death the court mourned for three days.

sentences.zh: 惠性寬厚，自奉儉薄。

translations.literal: Hui's nature was generous and mild, and his personal manner of living was frugal.
translations.idiomatic: Hui was generous of temperament and lived modestly.

sentences.zh: 興宗使惠恣取珍物，惠曰：「臣以戚屬據要地，祿足養廉，奴婢千餘，不為闕乏。

translations.literal: Emperor Xingzong had Hui take precious objects at will; Hui said: "Your servant, as an imperial kinsman holding a vital post, has salary enough to sustain integrity; I have more than a thousand slaves and servants and am not in want.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xingzong urged him to help himself to treasures; Hui replied, "As imperial kin in high office, my stipend suffices for honest living, and with more than a thousand servants I want for nothing.

sentences.zh: 陛下猶有所賜，貧於臣者何以待之。」

translations.literal: If Your Majesty still gives to me, how will those poorer than your servant be treated?"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty still bestows gifts on me, what hope have men poorer than I?"

sentences.zh: 帝以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor considered this right.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 故為將雖數敗衄，不之罪也。

translations.literal: Therefore though as a general he suffered defeat several times, he was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Hence although he suffered several defeats as a commander, he was never punished.

sentences.zh: 弟虛列，武定軍節度使。

translations.literal: His younger brother Xulie was Military Commissioner of the Wuding Army.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xulie served as military commissioner of the Wuding Army.

sentences.zh: 二子：慈氏奴，兀古匿。

translations.literal: Two sons: Cishinu and Wuguni.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Cishinu and Wuguni.

sentences.zh: 兀古匿終北府宰相。

translations.literal: Wuguni ended as chancellor of the Northern Court.
translations.idiomatic: Wuguni eventually became chancellor of the Northern Court.

sentences.zh: 慈氏奴字寧隱。

translations.literal: Cishinu was styled Ningyin.
translations.idiomatic: Cishinu, styled Ningyin.

sentences.zh: 太平初，以戚屬補祗候郎君。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping, by virtue of imperial kinship he was appointed Attendant Gentleman of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiping era he entered service as an attendant gentleman through his imperial connections.

sentences.zh: 上愛其勤慎，升閘撒狘，加右監門衛上將軍。

translations.literal: The emperor prized his diligence and prudence, promoted him to zhisanu, and additionally appointed him Right Senior General of the Jianmen Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued his diligence and discretion, raised him to zhisanu, and made him a senior general of the Right Jianmen Guard.

sentences.zh: 西邊有警，授西北路招討都監，領保大軍節度使。

translations.literal: When the western frontier sounded alarm, he was appointed Northwestern Route Pacification Supervisory Commissioner and concurrently Military Commissioner of the Baoda Army.
translations.idiomatic: When trouble arose on the western frontier, he was named supervisory commissioner for northwestern pacification and military commissioner of the Baoda Army.

sentences.zh: 政濟恩威，諸部悅附。

translations.literal: His governance combined favor and authority, and the tribes were pleased and attached.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with both kindness and force, and the tribes gladly submitted.

sentences.zh: 入為殿前副點檢，歷烏古敵烈部詳穩。

translations.literal: He entered court as Deputy Front Palace Inspector and served as xiangwen of the Wugu and Dilie tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to court as deputy front palace inspector and later served as xiangwen over the Wugu and Dilie tribes.

sentences.zh: 征李諒祚，為統軍都監，與西北路招討使敵魯古率蕃部諸軍由北路趨涼州，獲諒祚親屬。

translations.literal: Campaigning against Li Liangzuo, he served as Army Supervisory Commissioner; with Northwestern Route Pacification Commissioner Dilugu he led the various tribal armies of the frontier north toward Liangzhou and captured Liangzuo's kin.
translations.idiomatic: In the campaign against Li Liangzuo he served as army supervisory commissioner; with Dilugu, the northwestern pacification commissioner, he led the frontier tribal forces north toward Liangzhou and took Liangzuo's relatives prisoner.

sentences.zh: 夏人扼險以拒，慈氏奴中流矢卒，年五十一，贈中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: The Xia people barred the passes to resist; Cishinu was struck by a flying arrow and died at fifty-one; he was posthumously granted Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia held the mountain passes against them; Cishinu took an arrow and died at fifty-one, and was posthumously made grand councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 蕭迂魯，字胡突堇，五院部人。

translations.literal: Xiao Yulu, styled Hutujin, was a man of the Wuyuan Division.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Yulu, whose courtesy name was Hutujin, came from the Wuyuan Division.

sentences.zh: 父約質，歷官節度使。

translations.literal: His father Yuezhi held successive posts as military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuezhi had served as military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 迂魯重熙間為牌印郎君。

translations.literal: Yulu during the Chongxi era served as Seal and Credential Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongxi period Yulu served as seal and credential gentleman.

sentences.zh: 清寧九年，國家既平重元之亂，其黨郭九等亡，詔迂魯追捕，獲之，遷護衛太保。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Qingning, after the state had pacified the rebellion of Chongyuan, his partisans Guo Jiu and others fled; an edict ordered Yulu to pursue and capture them; he did so and was transferred to Grand Guardian of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Qingning year 9, after the Chongyuan rebellion was crushed, fugitives such as Guo Jiu were ordered hunted down; Yulu captured them and was promoted to grand guardian of the guard.

sentences.zh: 咸雍元年，使宋議邊事，稱旨，知殿前副點檢事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianyong he was sent to Song to negotiate border affairs; his mission pleased the throne, and he was appointed to manage the office of Deputy Front Palace Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianyong year 1 he was sent to Song on border negotiations; the mission pleased the throne, and he was put in charge of the deputy front palace inspectorate.

sentences.zh: 五年，阻卜叛，為行軍都監，擊敗之，俘獲甚眾。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Zhibu rebelled; he served as campaign supervisory commissioner, defeated them, and captured a great multitude.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5, when the Zhibu rebelled, he served as campaign supervisory commissioner, routed them, and took many captives.

sentences.zh: 初，軍出止給五月糧，過期糧乏，士卒往往叛歸。

translations.literal: At first when the army set out only five months' grain was issued; when the term expired and grain ran short, soldiers often deserted and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Originally the troops were rationed for only five months; when supplies ran out, many soldiers deserted home.

sentences.zh: 迂魯坐失計，免官，降戍西北部。

translations.literal: Yulu was judged for faulty planning, dismissed from office, and demoted to garrison duty in the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: Yulu was stripped of office for poor planning and sent to garrison the northwest.

sentences.zh: 未行，會北部兵起，迂魯將烏古敵烈兵擊敗之，每戰以身先，由是釋前罪，命總知烏古敵烈部。

translations.literal: Before he departed, trouble broke out in the north; Yulu led Wugu and Dilie troops to defeat the rebels; in every battle he took the lead in person; thereby his former offense was pardoned and he was ordered to govern the Wugu and Dilie tribes in general.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave, an uprising broke out in the north; Yulu led Wugu and Dilie forces to victory, fighting at the front in every engagement; his earlier fault was forgiven and he was placed in overall charge of the Wugu and Dilie tribes.

sentences.zh: 九年，敵烈叛，都監耶律獨叠以兵少不戰，屯臚朐河。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Dilie rebelled; Supervisory Commissioner Yelu Dudie, finding his troops too few to fight, encamped on the Luchu River.
translations.idiomatic: In year 9, when the Dilie rebelled, supervisory commissioner Yelu Dudie held the Luchu River with too few men to engage.

sentences.zh: 敵烈合邊人掠居民，迂魯率精騎四百力戰，敗之，盡獲其輜重。

translations.literal: The Dilie combined with frontier people to plunder residents; Yulu led four hundred elite horsemen and fought fiercely, defeated them, and captured all their baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: The Dilie joined with frontier raiders to plunder settlements; Yulu charged with four hundred picked cavalry, routed them, and seized their entire baggage train.

sentences.zh: 繼聞酋長合術三千餘騎掠附近部落，縱兵躡其後，連戰二日，斬數千級，盡得被掠人畜而還。

translations.literal: Later he heard the chieftain Heshu with more than three thousand horsemen was plundering nearby tribes; he unleashed his troops to follow in their tracks; fighting two days in succession he beheaded several thousand, recovered all the people and livestock taken, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that chieftain Heshu was raiding neighboring tribes with more than three thousand horsemen, he pursued them for two days of fighting, took thousands of heads, recovered all captives and livestock, and returned.

sentences.zh: 值敵烈黨五百餘騎劫捕鷹戶，逆擊走之，俘斬甚眾，自是敵烈勢沮。

translations.literal: He encountered more than five hundred horsemen of the Dilie faction raiding eagle-keepers; he met and struck them and drove them off, capturing and killing a great multitude; from this the Dilie power waned.
translations.idiomatic: He intercepted more than five hundred Dilie riders looting the falconers' camps, drove them off with heavy losses, and from then on Dilie strength collapsed.

sentences.zh: 時敵烈方為邊患，而阻卜相繼寇掠，邊人以故疲弊。

translations.literal: At that time the Dilie were just then a frontier trouble, and the Zhibu in succession raided and plundered; because of this the frontier people were worn and distressed.
translations.idiomatic: The Dilie were then the chief frontier threat, and Zhibu raids followed one after another until the border people were exhausted.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以地遠，不能時益援軍，而使疆圉帖然者，皆迂魯力也。

translations.literal: The court, because the region was distant, could not timely increase relief troops, yet the frontier remained secure—this was all Yulu's effort.
translations.idiomatic: Though the court could not promptly reinforce so distant a frontier, the border stayed quiet—entirely through Yulu's exertions.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉其功，拜左皮室詳穩。

translations.literal: The emperor praised his merit and appointed him Left Pishi xiangwen.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rewarded his service with appointment as Left Pishi xiangwen.

sentences.zh: 會宋求天池之地，詔迂魯兼統兩皮室軍屯太牢古山以備之。

translations.literal: When Song sought the land of Tianchi, an edict ordered Yulu concurrently to command both Pishi armies and encamp at Tailaogu Mountain to guard against this.
translations.idiomatic: When Song pressed a claim to Tianchi, Yulu was ordered to take command of both Pishi armies and encamp at Tailaogu Mountain in readiness.

sentences.zh: 大康初，阻卜叛，遷西北招討都監，從都統耶律趙三征討有功，改南京統軍都監、黃皮室詳穩。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dakang the Zhibu rebelled; he was transferred to Northwestern Pacification Supervisory Commissioner; following Commander-in-Chief Yelu Zhaosan on punitive expedition he had merit; he was changed to Southern Capital Army Supervisory Commissioner and Yellow Pishi xiangwen.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Dakang era, when the Zhibu rebelled, he became northwestern pacification supervisory commissioner; campaigning under commander-in-chief Yelu Zhaosan he distinguished himself and was made southern capital army supervisory commissioner and Yellow Pishi xiangwen.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷東北路統軍都監，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Northeast Route Army Supervisory Commissioner and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was transferred to northeastern route army supervisory commissioner and died in office.

sentences.zh: 弟鐸盧斡。

translations.literal: Younger brother Duoluwo.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Duoluwo.

sentences.zh: 鐸盧斡，字撒板。

translations.literal: Duoluwo, styled Saban.
translations.idiomatic: Duoluwo, whose courtesy name was Saban.

sentences.zh: 幼警悟異常兒。

translations.literal: As a child he was alert and perceptive beyond ordinary children.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a child he showed an unusual quickness of mind.

sentences.zh: 三歲失母，哭盡哀，見者傷之。

translations.literal: At three he lost his mother; he wept with utmost grief, and those who saw it were moved.
translations.idiomatic: When he lost his mother at three, he wept with such grief that all who saw him were moved.

sentences.zh: 及長，魁偉沈毅，好學，善屬文，有才幹。

translations.literal: When grown he was imposing and grave, loved learning, was skilled at literary composition, and had talent and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Grown to manhood he was tall and steady, devoted to learning, gifted in prose, and capable in affairs.

sentences.zh: 年三十始仕，為朝野推重，給事北院知聖旨事。

translations.literal: He did not enter office until thirty; court and commonwealth alike respected him; he served in the Northern Court office managing imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service only at thirty, already esteemed at court and beyond, and served in the Northern Court office for imperial edicts.

sentences.zh: 大康二年，乙辛再入樞府，鐸盧斡素與蕭巖壽善，誣以罪，謫戍西北部。

translations.literal: In the second year of Dakang, when Yixin again entered the Privy Council, Duoluwo had long been on good terms with Xiao Yanshou; he was slandered with a crime and banished to garrison the northwest.
translations.idiomatic: In Dakang year 2, when Yixin returned to the Privy Council, Duoluwo—who had long been close to Xiao Yanshou—was framed and sent to garrison the northwest.

sentences.zh: 坐皇太子事，特恩減死，仍錮終身。

translations.literal: Because of the crown prince affair he was granted special favor and had death reduced; still he was imprisoned for life.
translations.idiomatic: Implicated in the crown prince affair, he was spared death by special grace but imprisoned for life.

sentences.zh: 在戍十餘年，太子事稍直，始得歸鄉里，屏居謝人事。

translations.literal: In garrison for more than ten years, when the crown prince affair was gradually cleared he was at last able to return to his native place and lived in seclusion, declining human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten years in exile, as the crown prince's case gradually cleared, he returned home and withdrew from public life.

sentences.zh: 一日臨流，聞雉鳴，三復孔子「時哉」語，作古詩三章見誌。

translations.literal: One day by the stream he heard a pheasant call, thrice repeated Confucius's words "The timely one!" and composed three old-style poems to express his intent.
translations.idiomatic: One day beside a stream he heard a pheasant cry, repeated three times Confucius's remark on timeliness, and wrote three old-style poems to mark his thoughts.

sentences.zh: 當時名士稱其高情雅韻，不減古人。

translations.literal: Men of distinction of the time praised his lofty sentiment and elegant tone as not falling short of the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporary men of letters praised his refined spirit and literary grace as the equal of the ancients.

sentences.zh: 壽隆六年卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Shoulong he died at sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Shoulong year 6 at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 乾統初，贈彰義軍節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiantong he was posthumously granted Military Commissioner of the Zhangyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qiantong era he was posthumously made military commissioner of the Zhangyi Army.

sentences.zh: 蕭圖玉，字兀衍，北府宰相海璃之子。

translations.literal: Xiao Tuyu, styled Wuyan, was son of Northern Court Chancellor Haili.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Tuyu, whose courtesy name was Wuyan, was the son of Northern Court chancellor Haili.

sentences.zh: 統和初，皇太后稱制，以戚屬入侍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tonghe, when the empress dowager held regency, he entered attendance by virtue of imperial kinship.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tonghe era, when the empress dowager held regency, he entered court service through imperial connections.

sentences.zh: 尋為烏古部都監。

translations.literal: Soon he became Supervisory Commissioner of the Wugu Tribe.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made supervisory commissioner of the Wugu tribe.

sentences.zh: 討速母縷等部有功，遷烏古部節度使。

translations.literal: Campaigning against the Sumulü and other tribes he had merit and was transferred to Military Commissioner of the Wugu Tribe.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in campaigns against Sumulü and other tribes he was promoted to military commissioner of the Wugu tribe.

sentences.zh: 十九年，總領西北路軍事。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he took overall charge of Northwestern Route military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 he assumed overall command of northwestern military affairs.

sentences.zh: 後以本路兵伐甘州，降其酋長牙懶。

translations.literal: Later with the troops of this route he attacked Ganzhou and caused its chieftain Yalan to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Later he led the route's army against Ganzhou and forced chieftain Yalan to surrender.

sentences.zh: 既而牙懶復叛，命討之，克肅州，盡遷其民於土隗口故城。

translations.literal: Before long Yalan rebelled again; he was ordered to subdue him, took Suzhou, and moved all its people to the old city at Tuweikou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yalan rebelled again, he was ordered to suppress him, captured Suzhou, and resettled the entire population in the old city at Tuweikou.

sentences.zh: 師還，詔尚金鄉公主，拜駙馬都尉，加同政事令門下平章事。

translations.literal: When the army returned, an edict matched him with the Princess of Jinxiang; he was appointed Commandant Escort and additionally made Associate Director of the Directorate of Affairs and Grand Councilor of the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was matched with the Princess of Jinxiang, made commandant escort, and given the concurrent titles of associate director of the directorate of affairs and grand councilor of the chancellery.

sentences.zh: 上言曰：「阻卜今已服化，宜各分部，治以節度使。」

translations.literal: He submitted memorial saying: "The Zhibu have now submitted to civilization; they should be divided into separate departments and governed by military commissioners."
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne: "Now that the Zhibu have submitted, they should be divided into separate divisions and governed by military commissioners."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 自後節度使往往非材，部民怨而思叛。

translations.literal: Afterward the military commissioners were often men without ability; the tribes resented this and thought of rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the commissioners were often unfit men, and the tribes grew resentful and restless.

sentences.zh: 開泰元年十一月，石烈太師阿裏底殺其節度使，西奔窩魯朵城，蓋古所謂龍庭單于城也。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Kaitai, Shilie Grand Preceptor Alidi killed his military commissioner and fled west to Woluduo City—this was the ancient so-called Dragon Court Chanyu City.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Kaitai year 1, Grand Preceptor Alidi of the Shilie killed his military commissioner and fled west to Woluduo—the ancient Dragon Court of the Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 已而阻卜復叛，圍圖玉於可敦城，勢甚張。

translations.literal: Before long the Zhibu rebelled again and besieged Tuyu at Keden City; their momentum was very strong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Zhibu rebelled again and besieged Tuyu at Keden with overwhelming force.

sentences.zh: 圖玉使諸軍齊射卻之，屯於窩魯朵城。

translations.literal: Tuyu had the armies shoot together and repelled them, then encamped at Woluduo City.
translations.idiomatic: Tuyu had his troops fire in unison and drive them back, then encamped at Woluduo.

sentences.zh: 明年，北院樞密使耶律化哥引兵來救，圖玉遣人誘諸部皆降。

translations.literal: The next year Northern Court Privy Councilor Yelu Huage led troops to the rescue; Tuyu sent men to entice the tribes and all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Northern Court privy councilor Yelu Huage marched to relieve him; Tuyu sent envoys to win over the tribes, and all surrendered.

sentences.zh: 帝以圖玉始雖失計，後得人心，釋之，仍領諸部。

translations.literal: The emperor held that though Tuyu at first had miscalculated, afterward he won men's hearts; he pardoned him and still left him in charge of the tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Though Tuyu had blundered at first, the emperor pardoned him for winning the tribes' loyalty afterward and left him in command.

sentences.zh: 請益軍，詔讓之曰：「叛者既服，兵安用益？

translations.literal: He requested increased troops; an edict rebuked him saying: "The rebels have already submitted—what use is there in increasing troops?
translations.idiomatic: When he asked for reinforcements, an edict rebuked him: "The rebels have already submitted—why add troops?

sentences.zh: 且前日之役，死傷甚眾，若從汝謀，邊事何時而息？」

translations.literal: Moreover in the engagement the other day deaths and wounds were very numerous; if your plan were followed, when would frontier affairs ever cease?"
translations.idiomatic: And the last battle cost us dearly—if I followed your counsel, when would the frontier ever know peace?"

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: Thereupon it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 會公主坐殺家婢，降封郡主，圖玉罷使相。

translations.literal: Then the princess was judged for killing a household maid; her rank was reduced to commandery princess; Tuyu was removed from commissioner and chancellor posts.
translations.idiomatic: When the princess was punished for killing a servant, she was demoted to commandery princess and Tuyu was stripped of his commissioner and chancellor titles.

sentences.zh: 尋起為烏古敵烈部詳穩。

translations.literal: Soon he was raised again as xiangwen of the Wugu and Dilie tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon restored as xiangwen over the Wugu and Dilie tribes.

sentences.zh: 以老代還，卒。

translations.literal: Because of age he was replaced and returned; he died.
translations.idiomatic: He was relieved on account of age, returned home, and died.

sentences.zh: 子雙古，南京統軍使。

translations.literal: Son Shuanggu was Southern Capital Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shuanggu served as military commissioner of the Southern Capital.

sentences.zh: 孫訛篤斡，尚三韓郡王合魯之女骨浴公主，終烏古敵烈部統軍使，以善戰名於世。

translations.literal: Grandson Eduohe married Princess Guyu, daughter of Prince of Sanhan Commandery Helu; he ended as Army Commissioner of the Wugu and Dilie tribes and was famed in the world for skill in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Eduohe married Princess Guyu, daughter of the Prince of Sanhan Commandery, Helu; he ultimately served as army commissioner of the Wugu and Dilie tribes and won renown throughout the realm as a fighter.

sentences.zh: 耶律鐸軫，字敵輦，積慶宮人。

translations.literal: Yelu Duozhen, styled Dilian, was a man of the Jiqing Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yelu Duozhen, whose courtesy name was Dilian, came from the Jiqing Palace faction.

sentences.zh: 仕統和間。

translations.literal: He served during the Tonghe era.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service during the Tonghe period.

sentences.zh: 性疏簡，不顧小節，人初以是短之。

translations.literal: His nature was loose and simple; he did not heed small proprieties; people at first faulted him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Careless in manner and heedless of minor decorum, he was at first criticized for it.

sentences.zh: 後侵宋，分總羸師以從。

translations.literal: Later invading Song, he was put in charge of a division of depleted troops to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on the Song campaign, he was given command of a weakened detachment.

sentences.zh: 及戰，取緋帛被介胄以自標顯，馳突出入敵陣，格殺甚眾。

translations.literal: When battle came he took crimson silk to cover his armor for self-display, charged in and out of the enemy ranks, and killed a great multitude in close combat.
translations.idiomatic: In battle he draped crimson silk over his armor to make himself conspicuous, then charged repeatedly through the enemy lines and killed many in hand-to-hand fighting.

sentences.zh: 太后望見喜，召謂之曰：「卿戮力如此，何患不濟！」

translations.literal: The empress dowager saw this from afar and was pleased; she summoned him and said: "You exert yourself thus—what fear is there of failure!"
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager saw him from afar and was delighted; summoning him she said, "With such exertion as yours, how can we fail!"

sentences.zh: 厚賞之。

translations.literal: She richly rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: She rewarded him generously.

sentences.zh: 由是多以軍事屬任。

translations.literal: From this he was largely entrusted with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter military affairs were largely entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 俄授東北詳穩。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Northeast xiangwen.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Northeast xiangwen.

sentences.zh: 開泰二年，進討阻卜，克之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaitai he advanced to attack the Zhibu and conquered them.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaitai year 2 he marched against the Zhibu and subdued them.

sentences.zh: 重熙間，歷東北路統軍使、天德軍節度使。

translations.literal: During the Chongxi era he successively served as Northeast Route Military Commissioner and Military Commissioner of the Tiande Army.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chongxi period he served successively as northeastern route military commissioner and military commissioner of the Tiande Army.

sentences.zh: 十七年，城西邊，命鐸軫相地及造戰艦，因成樓船百三十艘。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year the western frontier was fortified; Duozhen was ordered to survey the terrain and build war vessels, thereby completing one hundred thirty tower ships.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17, while fortifying the western frontier, Duozhen was ordered to survey the terrain and build warships, completing one hundred thirty tower ships.

sentences.zh: 上置兵，下立馬，規制堅壯，稱旨。

translations.literal: Soldiers were placed above, horses stood below; the design was strong and solid, and it pleased the throne.
translations.idiomatic: With fighting decks above and horses stabled below, the design was stout and pleased the throne.

sentences.zh: 及西征，詔鐸軫率兵由別道進，會於河濱。

translations.literal: When the western expedition came, an edict ordered Duozhen to lead troops by a separate route and rendezvous at the riverbank.
translations.idiomatic: On the western expedition Duozhen was ordered to lead troops by a separate route and rendezvous at the river.

sentences.zh: 敵兵阻河而陣，帝御戰艦絕河擊之，大捷而歸，親賜卮酒。

translations.literal: Enemy troops blocked the river in battle array; the emperor himself manned a war vessel, crossed the river, and struck them; returning in great victory he personally bestowed a cup of wine.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy drew up across the river; the emperor crossed in a warship and routed them; on his triumphant return he personally offered Duozhen a cup of wine.

sentences.zh: 仍問所欲，鐸軫對曰：「臣幸被聖恩，得效駑力，萬死不能報國，又將何求！」

translations.literal: He further asked what he desired; Duozhen replied: "Your servant has fortunately received sacred grace and been able to offer humble strength; even ten thousand deaths could not repay the state—what more would I seek!"
translations.idiomatic: Asked what reward he wished, Duozhen replied, "I have been honored with imperial grace and offered what poor strength I have; a thousand deaths would not repay the state—what more could I ask?"

sentences.zh: 帝愈重之，手書鐸軫衣裙曰：「勤國忠君，舉世無雙。」

translations.literal: The emperor valued him all the more, and in his own hand wrote on Duozhen's coat and skirt: "Diligent in serving the state, loyal to the ruler—unmatched in the world."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor valued him the more and inscribed Duozhen's robe: "In service to the state and loyalty to the throne, unmatched under heaven."

sentences.zh: 卒於官，年七十。

translations.literal: He died in office at seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He passed away while in office, aged seventy.

sentences.zh: 子低烈，歷觀察、節度使。

translations.literal: Son Dilie successively served as observation commissioner and military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Dilie held successive posts as observation commissioner and military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 論曰：初，遼之謀復三關也，蕭惠贊伐宋之舉，而宋人增幣請和。

translations.literal: Commentary says: At first, when Liao planned to recover the Three Passes, Xiao Hui endorsed the campaign against Song, and the Song people increased tribute and sought peace.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators observe: When Liao first plotted to retake the Three Passes, Xiao Hui urged war on Song, and the Song court bought peace with increased tribute.

sentences.zh: 狃於一勝，移師西夏，而勇智俱廢，敗潰隨之。

translations.literal: Clinging to one victory, they shifted the army to Western Xia, and courage and wisdom alike were exhausted; defeat and rout followed.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk on a single victory, they turned against Western Xia until courage and judgment alike failed them, and defeat followed.

sentences.zh: 豈非貪小利、迷遠圖而然。

translations.literal: Was this not because of coveting small profit and losing sight of the long plan?
translations.idiomatic: Was this not the price of grasping at small gains while losing sight of the larger design?

sentences.zh: 況所得不償所亡，利果安在哉？

translations.literal: Moreover what was gained did not compensate for what was lost—where indeed was the profit?
translations.idiomatic: When gains could not offset losses, where was the profit to be found?

sentences.zh: 同時諸將撫綏邊圉，若迂魯忠勤不伐，鐸魯斡高情雅韻，鐸軫雖廉不逮蕭惠，而無邀功啟釁之罪，亦庶乎君子之風矣。

translations.literal: The generals of the same period who pacified and soothed the frontier: Yulu was loyal and diligent without boasting; Duoluwo had lofty sentiment and elegant tone; Duozhen, though integrity did not reach Xiao Hui's, yet had no crime of inviting merit and provoking strife—this also approximates the manner of a gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Among frontier commanders of the same era, Yulu served with loyal diligence and no self-aggrandizement; Duoluwo bore himself with refined integrity; and though Duozhen's modesty fell short of Xiao Hui's, none of them sought credit or provoked conflict—they came near, at least, to the mark of a gentleman.
